## Purpose

Record the assigned reviewer's fidelity verdict against the exact held batch revision
and live graph digest. Every active member section needs a verdict, together with
reverse coverage and walkthrough verdicts. Allowed verdicts are `faithful`, `fixed`
and `scope_question`.

## When a playbook uses it

The fidelity reviewer calls this after inspecting and correcting the held graph.
Any scope question prevents a passing receipt and opens a human scope ask. An answer
returns the batch to `held` for another edit and attestation round.

## How it works internally

`src/commands/fidelity_review_commands.py` checks the live assigned reviewer claim,
locks the graph, checks the expected revision and digest, and validates section
coverage. It freezes the source/design lineage and last diff alongside the findings.
`src/asks/batch_scope.py` adapts unresolved scope questions to the generic ask boundary.

## Side effects and persistence

Writes `ingest_batch_receipts` and moves the batch to `reviewing` for a pass or
`needs_scope` for a scope question. Scope asks use the source key
`batch-scope:<batch_id>:<revision>`. Durable outbox events are
`batch.receipt_recorded` and `batch.needs_scope`. Identical retries reuse the receipt
and ask. Neither attestation nor a scope answer clears any member hold or releases work.

## Failure modes and diagnostics

`not_authorized` means the live assigned reviewer no longer holds authority.
`stale_revision` requires rereading the batch and its live digest.
`incomplete_review` lists uncovered sections. `needs_scope` requires applying the
pending human answer before a fresh pass. An existing passing receipt cannot be
replaced; an existing scope question cannot be rewritten within the same revision.

## Example step

Call `task_batch_review_record` with the inspected batch id, structure revision and
digest; bind the result as `receipt`. Supply `section_verdicts` covering every active
section, `reverse_coverage_verdict` and `walkthrough_verdict` as `faithful` after
confirming coverage, and `structural_findings` as the recorded findings (or `[]`).
On `recorded`, continue the review policy; on `needs_scope`, await the human answer
and inspect the graph again. Handle `rejected` visibly without releasing members.
